title: Table has no accessible caption or aria-label — screen readers see an unlabeled data table
detail: Lines 253-303: the <table className="dcfg-table"> has no <caption>, aria-label, or aria-describedby. Screen readers announce 'table with 8 columns' with no context about what data the table represents. The sortable column headers use onClick but have no role="columnheader" aria-sort attributes, so screen readers cannot convey sort state. Same pattern seen in other list screens but worth cataloging here for completeness.
evidence: Onboarding.jsx:253 `<table className="dcfg-table">` — no caption or aria-label. Lines 257-264: <th> elements use onClick for sorting but no aria-sort.
recommendedFix: Add `aria-label="Onboarding cases"` to the <table>. On each sortable <th>, add `aria-sort={sortCol === 'colName' ? (sortDir === 'asc' ? 'ascending' : 'descending') : 'none'}`. This is a shared pattern — consider updating useTableControls to emit aria-sort props alongside SortIcon.

title: NewCasePanel overlay has no focus trap — keyboard users can tab behind the modal
detail: Lines 328-362: NewCasePanel renders a fixed overlay with a side panel. There is no focus trap — pressing Tab from the Save button cycles focus behind the overlay to the main page buttons and table rows. No onKeyDown handler for Escape to close. The overlay div also has no role="dialog" or aria-modal attributes. For external testers using keyboard navigation, the modal is effectively invisible to assistive tech.
evidence: Onboarding.jsx:328-362 — overlayStyle positions the panel but no focus management. No role='dialog', no aria-modal='true', no Escape handler.
recommendedFix: Add role='dialog' aria-modal='true' to the panel div (line 329). Add an onKeyDown={e => e.key === 'Escape' && onClose()} handler on the overlay. For focus trapping, either use a lightweight trap (tabindex management on mount) or adopt the existing SlideOutPanel component which already handles this. SlideOutPanel is imported in other screens — reusing it here would be the most consistent approach.

title: handleNewCase case-number generation has a race condition — concurrent users can mint the same OB-YYYY-NNN
detail: Lines 107-163: handleNewCase reads the highest existing case number, increments it client-side, then checks for duplicates before creating. Between the read (line 111) and the dup-check (line 119), another user can mint the same number. The dup-check itself is also racy — by the time the POST executes, the dup check is stale. The current mitigation (lines 119-124) silently swallows the collision by closing the panel and reloading. But the user sees no feedback that their case was NOT created. For single-user testing this is fine; for concurrent external testers creating cases simultaneously, they can get phantom 'success' with no case created.
evidence: Onboarding.jsx:111 reads max case number. :119 checks for dup. :127 creates — any of these three steps can race against a concurrent user.
recommendedFix: Catalog-only for this review. Long-term fix: move case-number generation server-side (auto-number column in Dataverse, or a Power Automate flow that assigns the number on create). Short-term mitigation: if the dup-check finds a collision, toast the user with 'Case number conflict — please retry' instead of silently closing the panel.

title: Case number parsing uses split('-')[2] without validation — NaN propagates on malformed case numbers
detail: Line 115: `const nextNum = last ? String(parseInt(last.split('-')[2]) + 1).padStart(3, '0') : '001';` — if any existing case number doesn't follow the OB-YYYY-NNN pattern (e.g., a manually created case with dcfg_case_number='OB-2026'), `split('-')[2]` returns undefined, parseInt returns NaN, NaN + 1 = NaN, and the new case number becomes 'OB-2026-NaN'. The apiPost would succeed creating a case with a garbled number.
evidence: Onboarding.jsx:115 — no guard on parseInt result.
recommendedFix: Add a guard: `const parsed = parseInt(last.split('-')[2]); const nextNum = (!isNaN(parsed)) ? String(parsed + 1).padStart(3, '0') : '001';`. This falls back to 001 if the highest existing case number is malformed.

title: NewCasePanel fetchCustomers failure hides the error — user sees empty dropdown with no explanation
detail: Lines 321-324: `fetchCustomers().then(r => { setCustomers(r?.value ?? []); setLoadingCust(false); }).catch(() => setLoadingCust(false));` — if fetchCustomers fails (403, network, etc.), the catch clears the loading state and the panel renders an empty dropdown with just 'Select customer...' and no error message. The user has no way to know customers failed to load vs. there being zero customers.
evidence: Onboarding.jsx:322-324 — .catch(() => setLoadingCust(false)) swallows the error entirely.
recommendedFix: Add a local error state in the catch: `.catch((err) => { setLoadingCust(false); /* show inline error */ })`. Display 'Failed to load customers' in place of the dropdown. Or use toast from the parent scope. Since the panel is already modal, inline feedback is better UX.

title: Intake session status uses hardcoded magic number 100000000 without named constant
detail: Lines 567-568: `intakeSession.dcfg_status === 100000000 ? 'badge-green' : 'badge-grey'` and `intakeSession.dcfg_status === 100000000 ? 'Active' : 'Complete'` — the Dataverse option-set value 100000000 is used raw. Also at line 387: `dcfg_status: 100000000` in the apiPost body. These should reference a named constant from portalApi.js (like OnboardingCaseStatus does for case statuses). If the option-set changes or a new status is added, grep for '100000000' won't find an unambiguous match.
evidence: OnboardingDetail.jsx:567, 568, 387 — three raw uses of 100000000 for intake session status.
recommendedFix: Add `export const IntakeSessionStatus = { Active: 100000000, Complete: 100000001 };` to portalApi.js (verify the actual option-set values from the schema). Replace the three raw references in OnboardingDetail.jsx with the named constant.

title: StepDetailPanel dependency_type uses magic numbers 100000001/100000002 without named constants
detail: Lines 858-859: `step.dcfg_dependency_type === 100000001 ? 'Start-to-Start' : step.dcfg_dependency_type === 100000002 ? 'Start-to-Finish' : 'Finish-to-Start'` — three raw option-set values. Same pattern issue as CR-1005. These should use a named enum from portalApi.js.
evidence: OnboardingDetail.jsx:858-859 — raw option-set magic numbers for dependency type.
recommendedFix: Add `export const DependencyType = { FinishToStart: 100000000, StartToStart: 100000001, StartToFinish: 100000002 };` to portalApi.js. Replace the ternary chain with a lookup object.

title: beforeunload dirty guard works for browser close but not for in-app navigation — HashRouter navigation bypasses it
detail: Lines 184-188: the beforeunload event listener correctly guards against closing the browser tab with unsaved changes. However, the SPA uses HashRouter, and in-app navigation (clicking a nav link, breadcrumb back to /onboarding, etc.) does NOT trigger beforeunload. The dirty state guard only fires on browser-level close/refresh. An external tester who edits case fields then clicks 'Onboarding' in the breadcrumb (line 449) will lose all changes silently. react-router v6 removed the Prompt component; the standard workaround is useBlocker() or a custom beforeNavigate guard.
evidence: OnboardingDetail.jsx:184-188 — window.addEventListener('beforeunload'). Line 449: Link to=/onboarding that navigates away without checking dirty.
recommendedFix: Add a useBlocker() guard (react-router v6.4+) or implement a custom navigation guard that checks `dirty` and shows a confirmation dialog before allowing in-app navigation. The existing dirty state and Save button are already in place — just needs the router-level guard.

title: copyIntakeLink has no error handling — clipboard API can fail silently
detail: Lines 400-407: `navigator.clipboard.writeText(text).then(() => { ... })` — the .then() handles success but there is no .catch(). If the clipboard API is denied (some browsers require secure context or user gesture), the promise rejects unhandled. The user clicks 'Copy Link + Code', nothing happens, no feedback. Also, if the browser does not support navigator.clipboard (older WebView, Power Pages embedded), this will throw immediately.
recommendedFix: Add `.catch(() => { toast?.show('err', 'Copy failed — please copy manually'); })`. Optionally add a fallback using document.execCommand('copy') for legacy environments, though this is low priority since Power Pages on dmms1 runs in modern browsers.

title: handleSave does not disable action buttons atomically — Close Case and Delete are clickable during save
detail: Lines 190-221: handleSave sets `setSaving(true)` at the top, but the Close Case button (line 463) and Delete button (line 466) both check `disabled={saving}`. If saving is already true from a handleSave in flight, they are correctly disabled. However, handleClose (line 223) and handleDeleteCase (line 267) each independently set `setSaving(true)`. There is no mutex — a fast double-click on 'Close Case' while a save is mid-flight could enqueue a close before the save finishes, potentially posting a status change before the PATCH from handleSave completes, leading to stale data overwriting the save.
evidence: OnboardingDetail.jsx:190 handleSave, :223 handleClose, :267 handleDeleteCase — all set saving=true but no guard against concurrent invocation while another op is in-flight.
recommendedFix: Add an early-return guard at the top of each handler: `if (saving) return;`. The existing `disabled={saving}` on buttons provides the primary guard, but the early-return prevents programmatic double-invocation and is a standard defense-in-depth pattern.

title: EditableText and EditableField initialize draft from props but never sync when props change after loadCase()
detail: Lines 1128-1149 (EditableText) and 1152-1173 (EditableField): both components use `useState(value)` to initialize their draft state from props. After loadCase() refetches and re-renders the parent, these components receive new `value` props but their internal `draft` state retains the old value (React useState initializer only runs on mount). This means: (1) user edits a note and blurs (triggering save), (2) loadCase() fires and returns the updated value, (3) the EditableText re-renders but still shows the pre-save draft, not the server value. The visual desync is minor because the values are usually identical post-save, but if the server normalizes the value differently (trim, etc.), the field shows stale content until the component unmounts and remounts.
recommendedFix: Add a useEffect to sync draft with prop changes: `useEffect(() => { setDraft(value); }, [value]);`. Low priority since the visual impact is minimal in practice.

title: Loading and error states return bare divs with no aria-live region — screen readers miss state transitions
detail: Lines 422-424: the loading skeleton, error banner, and null-case return paths are plain divs. When loadCase() completes and the content replaces the skeleton, screen readers have no notification mechanism. The error state (line 423) shows a warn-banner but no role='alert' so screen readers don't announce it. Applies to both Onboarding.jsx:212 (skeleton only) and OnboardingDetail.jsx.
evidence:
OnboardingDetail.jsx:422 `
`, :423 `
{error}
` — no aria-live or role='alert'.
recommendedFix: Add role='alert' to the error banner div. Wrap the main content area in an aria-live='polite' region so screen readers announce when content transitions from loading to loaded. Low priority for sighted external testers but matters for WCAG 2.1 compliance.

title: handleSave PATCHes the customer record with the full contactForm — can overwrite fields another user just saved
detail: Lines 206-215: handleSave PATCHes the customer record at `/${EntitySets.customers}(${custId})` with the entire contactForm object. If another user (or another screen like CustomerDetail) has updated a different customer field between the time this form loaded and the save fires, this PATCH overwrites it because it sends all 6 contact fields every time, even if only one changed. This is the 'last-write-wins' pattern on a shared entity. The case-level PATCH (lines 194-200) is safer because it only writes case fields that are exclusive to this screen.
evidence: OnboardingDetail.jsx:209 `await apiPatch(... , contactForm)` — sends all 6 fields on every save.
recommendedFix: Track which contact fields actually changed (e.g., a dirtyContactFields set) and only include those in the PATCH body. Alternatively, accept the last-write-wins behavior but document it as a known limitation — for the onboarding use case, these contact fields are primarily edited here, so the risk is low.

title: STATUS_DROPDOWN omits Closed status — case status dropdown has 5 options while CASE_STATUS_BADGE has 6
detail: Lines 1179-1185: STATUS_DROPDOWN defines 5 options (NotStarted through Complete). Line 43-50: CASE_STATUS_BADGE defines 6 entries including Closed. The status dropdown in the case form (line 491) doesn't include Closed because handleClose() is a separate action. However, if a case is reopened (handleReopen sets InProgress), the user cannot manually set it back to Closed via the dropdown — they must use the 'Close Case' button. This is intentional UX but creates an asymmetry that could confuse an external tester who expects the dropdown to cover all states.
recommendedFix: Catalog-only. The intentional exclusion of Closed from the dropdown is arguably correct (Closed is a lifecycle action, not a manual status pick). Add a comment above STATUS_DROPDOWN explaining why Closed is omitted.

title: handleCreateIntakeSession generates access code from Math.random() — predictable and collision-prone
detail: Lines 354-355: `const code = custName.replace(/[^A-Z0-9]/gi, '').substring(0, 4).toUpperCase() + Math.random().toString(36).substring(2, 6).toUpperCase();` — generates an 8-char access code using Math.random() which is not cryptographically secure and has a small but non-zero collision space (36^4 = ~1.7M possibilities for the random portion). For external-facing intake sessions used by customer contacts, this is an authentication credential. Collision means two customers could share an access code; predictability means someone could guess a code.
evidence: OnboardingDetail.jsx:354-355 — Math.random() for access code generation.
recommendedFix: Replace Math.random() with crypto.getRandomValues() for the random portion: `const arr = new Uint8Array(4); crypto.getRandomValues(arr); const code = prefix + Array.from(arr).map(b => b.toString(36)).join('').substring(0,4).toUpperCase();`. Also add a uniqueness check by querying existing sessions for the generated code before creating. Low risk for current user testing (few customers), but should be hardened before broader rollout.

title: PhaseCard and StepRow clickable divs are not keyboard-accessible — no tabIndex, role, or keyDown handler
detail: Line 703-704: PhaseCard header div has onClick={onTogglePhase} but no tabIndex='0', role='button', or onKeyDown handler. Same pattern at line 773-774 for StepRow. Keyboard-only users cannot expand/collapse phases or steps. The chevron SVGs are decorative-only with no button wrapper.
evidence: OnboardingDetail.jsx:703 `<div onClick={onTogglePhase} ...>` — no keyboard attributes. :773 `<div onClick={onToggle} ...>` — same.
recommendedFix: Add tabIndex={0}, role='button', and onKeyDown={e => { if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ') { e.preventDefault(); onTogglePhase(); } }} to both clickable divs. Add aria-expanded={expanded} to convey accordion state. This is the standard ARIA accordion pattern.

title: Table rows use onClick for navigation but have no keyboard affordance — not focusable or actionable via Enter
detail: Line 274: `<tr ... onClick={() => navigate(...)} style={{ cursor: 'pointer' }}>` — the entire row is clickable to navigate to the case detail. But <tr> elements are not focusable by default, and there is no tabIndex or role='link' to make them keyboard-accessible. A keyboard-only user cannot navigate to a case detail from the list screen without using the browser's spatial navigation (which is unreliable).
evidence: Onboarding.jsx:274 — <tr onClick=navigate> without tabIndex or keyboard handler.
recommendedFix: Add tabIndex={0} and onKeyDown={e => { if (e.key === 'Enter') navigate(...); }} to each <tr>. Add role='link' to communicate the navigation affordance to screen readers. Alternatively, wrap the case number cell content in a <Link> component for native keyboard and screen reader support.
